checks.message: Verify the environment is not using the default service role because it has broad permissions
checks.context: The default Elastic Beanstalk service role has AdministratorAccess-like permissions. Create a scoped role with only the permissions your environment actually needs.

checks.message: Verify HTTPS is configured. Beanstalk serves HTTP by default
checks.context: Default Beanstalk environments serve traffic over HTTP. Configure an HTTPS listener on the load balancer and redirect HTTP to HTTPS. Never serve production traffic unencrypted.

checks.message: Verify environment variables don't contain plaintext secrets
checks.context: Beanstalk environment variables are visible in the console and stored in plaintext. Anyone with elasticbeanstalk:DescribeConfigurationSettings can read them. Use Secrets Manager references instead.

checks.message: Termination deletes all environment resources including RDS if created by Beanstalk
checks.context: If you created an RDS instance through Beanstalk, terminating the environment deletes the database. Decouple your RDS from Beanstalk before terminating if you need to keep the data.

checks.message: Deleting an application removes all versions and environments permanently
checks.context: All application versions stored in S3 and all associated environments are destroyed. This cannot be undone. Terminate all environments first and verify no active traffic before deleting.

checks.message: Verify the source bundle doesn't contain hardcoded credentials or .env files
checks.context: Application bundles uploaded to S3 are accessible to anyone with S3 read access to that bucket. Scan your bundle for secrets before uploading. Git history, .env files, and config files are common culprits.
